LFM2.5-VL-450M, focused on large transferable units. 50 screens, 44 passed: 40 MLP families of 64 to 1024 units and 4 attention-head groups.

Method that worked: take a causal seed (an earlier screened unit, or the top-5 attribution units in one layer) and grow it with its weight neighbours. Neighbours are ranked by |cos| of the w1 gate row plus |cos| of the w2 output column against the seeds. Similarity to the seeds of confounding skills in the same layer is subtracted. That subtraction is what made the larger families pass: weekday removed from pronoun at L13, month removed from antonym at L8, antonym and comparative removed from month at L8, and the colour writer 515 removed from antonym at L13. Families mostly stay selective up to 512 units and beat random same-size parts.

- antonym: L8 at 64 (.778), 128 (.795), 256 (.766), 512 (.729, month subtracted) and 1024 (.737). L13 output stage at 128 (.182) and 256 (.201).

- multilingual: L2 heads [2,9,12,15] (.435) and [2,3,9,12,15] (.519). Random L2 5-head sets also drop multilingual by up to .48, so this is weaker evidence.
